body:
Oh, hmmm, what if the `li` is associated with a `ul` and it has `list-style: decimal` for example? I'm not sure whether this is in the scope of HTML or CSS Lists spec. Anyway, browsers agree on the same behavior on this case that `ul` are treated the same as `ol`, just with a different list style by default.

A more interesting case is that, what if the `li` is not associated with either `ol` or `ul`? In Gecko, the ordinal value would be zero, however WebKit (and Blink, which presumably inherits the behavior from WebKit) behaves as if there is an global level `ul` for `li` to associate to. Not sure whether this issue is important, though.

Per http://software.hixie.ch/utilities/js/live-dom-viewer/?saved=4633, Gecko does something weird where it displays a period but no number; Edge displays no prefix; and Chrome has the global counter behavior. Danggg. I guess I like Edge the most? _That_ probably belongs in CSS then; we can define such `<li>`s to have no ordinal value and then require that CSS display nothing, even with list-style-type set, for things with no ordinal value.
